item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00281","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C01","C11","C19"],"selected_candidate_label":"C01","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C01 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are Eisenhower veto memoranda concerning special financial relief for one municipality. Each first describes the particular municipal benefit, acknowledges that the claim appears fair when viewed narrowly, then rejects the bill because the community is not uniquely situated, comparable communities could seek the same treatment, and approval would create an undesirable precedent. C11 and C19 share the general special-treatment-versus-uniformity argument, but their drafting structures and factual settings are less closely aligned.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The original agreement was fair and Elkins has received and will continue to receive benefits at least proportionate to its relatively small share of the airport's total cost.","parent_excerpt":"Considered simply in terms of the specific facts, the claim for payment seems equitable.","explanation":"Both concede the apparent fairness of the individual municipality's claim before shifting to broader objections."},{"child_excerpt":"The bill would give special treatment to a single community and thereby discriminate against other communities","parent_excerpt":"But the claim covered in this bill is not unique, nor are the facts so peculiar and local that approval would set no precedent.","explanation":"The same core rationale rejects individualized municipal relief because similarly situated communities exist."},{"child_excerpt":"The bill would set a precedent which could be used by many other communities to urge cancellation of their obligations held by the Federal Government.","parent_excerpt":"if the bill is approved other communities may be expected to press similar--and perhaps equally meritorious--claims","explanation":"This is a close parallel in both language and administrative logic: relief for one city would invite comparable claims from other cities."}]}
